_purpose: What SHAPE of chat-completions request each model family accepts. The shipped mChatAI+ binary carries a frozen fallback (ModelRequestShapes.fallback in Swift); the runtime reads this file so a provider shipping a new family — which is what broke every OpenAI call on 2026-09-03 when gpt-5.6-luna rejected 'max_tokens' — is a same-day PR plus refreshMchataisourceCache, not an App Store cycle.
_why_this_is_content: The MODEL is already content: role-models.json and llm-catalog/providers/*.json pick which SKU a request uses, and openai.json already lists 70 gpt-5/o-series models. A one-line content change can therefore select a model the binary has never heard of. The rule for how to TALK to that model has to travel the same way, or content can break a shipped build with no way to fix it but a revert.
_matching: Rules are tried IN ORDER; the first whose provider matches and whose `modelPrefix` OR `minMajorVersion` matches wins. `modelPrefix` is a literal prefix on the lowercased model id. `family` + `minMajorVersion` matches ids like '<family>-<N>...' where N >= minMajorVersion, so a version nobody has released yet is still covered.

rules._notes: Split out of openai-reasoning for ONE reason: prompt_cache_retention has only ever been sent to gpt-4.1/o3/o4, and folding o1 in would smuggle a live behaviour change in under a refactor. If o1 does accept it, that is a one-word content flip.
o-series burn hidden reasoning tokens and reject temperature and response_format.
Does not think in the hidden way the o-series does, but shares the max_completion_tokens contract.

substituteForCodeGeneration is FALSE on purpose. The harness swaps o-series out for a code SKU because they answer a big-artifact ask with a short description; gpt-5 has no such record here, and turning it on would silently downgrade every gpt-5 user to gpt-4o. Flip it if evidence says otherwise. gpt-5 onward. Version-ranged rather than enumerated ON PURPOSE: gpt-5.6-luna was not on the enumerated list and every call 400'd. A gpt-6 nobody has announced is already covered.
The Messages API REQUIRES max_tokens. Never send max_completion_tokens here.
Google nests generationConfig; the token key lives there, not at the top level.

_outputTokenCaps: A CEILING on the completion budget, which is a different question from which KEY the budget travels under. AIHarness.maxCompletionTokens used to answer it with nine hasPrefix/contains tests compiled into the binary — over-spec 400s, under-spec truncates, and either way the only fix was a release. Rules are tried in order; `modelContains` rather than `modelPrefix` where the id arrives namespaced (bedrock 'anthropic.claude-...', openrouter 'anthropic/claude-...'). Numbers are deliberately CONSERVATIVE: a cap below the model's real limit costs a truncation the wizard already recovers from, a cap above it costs a hard 400.
_providerAliases: A proxy speaks its upstream's dialect. mChatAI Cloud and Azure OpenAI both serve OpenAI SKUs through an OpenAI-shaped endpoint, and the app's provider DISPLAY NAME ('mChatAI Cloud') matches no rule, so without this a Cloud user on gpt-5.6-luna falls to the default shape and 400s — the exact failure this file exists to stop. The literal name is tried first, so naming a proxy directly in `rules` still wins. Vertex AI and Amazon Bedrock are deliberately absent: they host models from more than one upstream, so a single alias would be a lie.

default._notes: Anything unmatched. Deliberately the LEGACY shape: an unknown model is more likely to be an OpenAI-compatible third party than a reasoning model, and the runtime 400-retry in LLMService corrects the guess and remembers it.
